title: Turmeric

seo.title: Turmeric (Haldi, Haridra) - Benefits, Uses and Safety
seo.description: Learn about turmeric, or haldi, including its botanical identity, Ayurvedic properties, traditional uses for throat and respiratory comfort, dosage and safety.

short_description: Turmeric is a golden rhizome traditionally used to support the throat, reduce Kapha stickiness and ease mild cough and congestion as part of kitchen Ayurveda.
full_description: Turmeric is the dried rhizome of Curcuma longa, known in Ayurveda as Haridra and in Hindi as haldi. It is bitter, pungent and heating, and is used both as a culinary spice and in traditional preparations for the throat and respiratory tract. A pinch in warm water, milk or with black pepper is a common household support during seasonal cough.

recommended_dosage.extract: Use only as directed by a qualified practitioner

ayurvedic_properties.dosha_effect: Traditionally considered balancing for Kapha and Pitta when used in moderate amounts; excess heat may aggravate Pitta.

key_benefits.benefit: Traditionally used to soothe a scratchy throat and mild cough.
May help reduce Kapha stickiness in the channels.
Used as a kitchen spice and in warm drinks during seasonal congestion.

therapeutic_uses.use: Traditionally used for Kasa, sore throat and Pratishyaya-related discomfort.
Used as a pinch in warm water, with honey after cooling, or with black pepper.
Used in gargles with warm water and a pinch of salt for throat irritation.

safety_and_contraindications.safety: High doses or extracts may irritate the stomach and are not a substitute for medical care.
People with gallstones, bile-duct obstruction, bleeding disorders, or those taking anticoagulant medicines should consult a clinician before using concentrated turmeric.
Avoid staining clothes and open wounds with culinary powder; stop use if allergy or significant discomfort occurs.
